title: JARVIS PC-skill school: local-model high school, paid-API college, graduation, proven by ground truth on fresh sandboxes
content: Give JARVIS safe control of the Windows PC as a package (jarvis_pc) plus one brain-facing tool module (tools/pcskills.py). Every action is classified T0 (automatic), T1 (reversible, journaled), T2 (always ask) or T3 (never) by a gate that is not weakened to make anything work. Installing from a GitHub link checks repo trust, downloads only a Windows release asset, verifies its checksum, Defender-scans it, checks signatures of the executables inside the extracted folder, installs and proves it landed, and rolls back on failure. Uninstall and cleanup move things into a quarantine folder (reversible); only purge deletes, per batch, after an explicit yes. Troubleshooting is read-only evidence gathering that ranks likely causes. The rule from the owner: API credits may be spent to master a skill but must never be needed to run it, so skills are stored as verified local playbooks. PC-skill school (jarvis_pc/school): 70 subjects graded against ground truth (system facts, files, services, apps, signatures, logs, ports, processes, windows, forms, Notepad, git repositories, a LibreOffice Calc sheet, a local stand-in web server, zip installs and uninstalls), mapped onto the owner's 26-area blueprint and 10-level ladder. Free local Ollama models teach first; Gemini (free, always on for the school) and Claude (school-only credits, capped per day) teach only what they could not. Teachers only write text; the permission gate classifies every command, lessons run unattended in throw-away sandboxes, and a skill is kept only after two offline exams on brand-new variants. UI skills (jarvis_pc/uiact) use a closed action language by control name, a gated executor bound to one window (UI Automation patterns; the cursor never moves), a native practice window whose own log is the ground truth, and the real Notepad launched by the school itself. Real third-party apps the person has open always need approval. Git (area 12): the gate now understands git -C <folder> (read-only subcommands status/log/branch/rev-list/rev-parse/show/diff are T0), still asks for anything that changes work, and treats git -c, --output, --ext-diff and -O as T2 because they can write a file or run a program; five school subjects are graded against real throw-away repositories. Owner decisions 2026-11-04: Claude's school cap raised to 15 a day; research and installs against local stand-ins approved. Gate: a plain GET of one page on this PC (127.0.0.1, localhost, [::1]) is T0 and Remove-Item is T1 only on a named path inside the allowed folders; every other fetch, wildcard or outside path still asks. The teacher prompt also states how to read a page or service on this PC, unpack a zip and remove a folder named in the task. (Lesson text for these lives in school/teachers.py RULES.) The UI teacher prompt says grid windows (spreadsheets) are driven by keyboard: key down/up/left/right, type, = formulas, key enter. Area 11 (programming) has three read-only lessons: the installed Python version, counting a requirements file, reading a project name. The teacher prompt also explains reading a program version and searching a file with Select-String. Area 24 starts with a lesson that finds the release file a stand-in project page offers. Area 22 (planning) has a four-step tidy-up lesson graded on the end state of the folders. Area 25 (accountability) has two lessons that read an audit log: how many actions, how many refused.
architecture: jarvis_pc/guardrails (gate, tiers, allowlist, audit, kill switch, ScopedApprover) -> jarvis_pc/actions/shell.py (gated runner) -> verify (checks, change journal with group ids, report) -> install, uninstall, diagnostics, files, perception, devenv, network, voice, learning. jarvis_pc/brain.py turns each risky skill into prepare() (read-only plan, key that changes if the plan changes) and run() (executes with an approver that accepts only the prompts the plan declared). tools/pcskills.py registers 11 tools in tools.ALL and DESK_ONLY and uses core.approvals so only the person's next real message can approve; the model cannot. It coexists with the already-merged PC control: install_program/uninstall_program (tools/software.py) keep ordinary programs and winget packages, pc_install handles GitHub links only, and software.uninstall_program hands an app JARVIS installed from GitHub to the reversible flow. The phone route (pcbridge.TOOLS) was deliberately not widened. jarvis_pc/school: curriculum.py, ui_subjects.py (tasks and ground truth), school.py (attempt, exam, study, phases, graduation, review, lock), teachers.py, local.py, cloud.py, live.py, transcript.py (report card, per-provider budget), blueprint.py, lock.py. jarvis_pc/uiact: lang.py, executor.py, uia.py, practice_app.py. Playbooks gained {placeholders} and kind=ui; core/scheduler.py studies every 20 minutes while the owner is away until graduated; tools/pcskills.py adds pc_school_status and pc_school_study (JARVIS_SCHOOL=off switches it off, and the skill smoke sandbox pins it off).
techniques: Plan first, run second: the plan text is what the person approves, and a hash of it is the approval key, so a yes cannot apply to a different plan. Group journal entries per run so undo reverts a whole install, including the downloaded zip. Quarantine instead of deleting. Treat all text from repos, READMEs, web pages and teacher models as untrusted data: scan it for prompt injection, classify every command with the gate, and keep a learned skill only after a verified run. A check that cannot run is reported as unproven, never as healthy; no checks run means FAIL. Prove properties with tests that try to break them: a plan altered after approval is refused, a rotted backup fails the restore test, a teacher is not called on the second run, a safety net stops tests from running real winget or deleting outside the temp folder. Ground truth that does not come from the command under test (Python facts, generated sandboxes, a practice window's log, a saved file). Decoy-aware grading. Exams on fresh variants, offline. Teacher text is untrusted: injection scan, tier check before anything runs, placeholders checked before tiers, an unattended guard that refuses every approval. Failures go back to the teacher as data. Reference answers prove each subject is solvable; each is graded on several random variants. Step trimming, a cross-process session lock, model rotation, and routing so no subject is left in limbo. UI lessons show the teacher what a person would see (the window's control names, digits masked) so it learns where to look, not the value.
mistakes: Undo reverted only the newest journal entry, leaving the downloaded zip behind; fixed with group ids. On Windows a new file's modified time can be slightly in the future, so 'any age' (0 days) randomly dropped brand-new items from cleanup and purge plans; age 0 must mean any age (found by stress-running a test 300 times). The shell runner caps output at 200000 characters and cut the head off the Application event log; truncated output must count as a failed check. Get-AuthenticodeSignature cannot take a folder, so extracted downloads answered 'unavailable' (a pass) and were never checked; signature_check_dir checks the files inside. A default argument named run inside a class resolved to the class's own method, not the shell runner. Spoken output such as 'event(s)' is rejected by the repo smoke test and needs real plurals and verb agreement. A unit test once reached the real shell and ran winget install; tests now run under a safety net, whose first version deadlocked because tempfile.gettempdir() deletes a probe file under a non-reentrant lock. A restore test that compares a backup only to its own copy cannot detect rot; it must compare against hashes recorded at backup time. Live runs showed local models copy the prompt's own example, so examples differ from every subject; Guardrails defaults to dry_run=True, which silently blocked every sandbox write; core.learn_llm points at LM Studio, so the school talks to Ollama directly; printing a whole folder passed 'which files' until decoys were graded; JARVIS_LOCAL_ONLY blocked every cloud lesson until the school got its own Gemini path; padded skills and a PASS-only tool result; two processes studying at once. UI Automation returns before the app handles the action (the grader waits to settle); Notepad's title gains * when unsaved (bind by window handle, clean up by file name); the parser once accepted ctrl+alt+delete; the skill smoke test could start a real study session. Git is T2 under the gate, so no git subjects. A rate-limited Gemini (HTTP 429) plus Claude's used-up daily cap made the Notepad read subject look stuck after four failed API tries; an unreachable teacher is now not a try, is refunded from the daily budget, and never flags a subject for a human. Windows 11 Notepad reopens every tab from its previous session, so each real-app run added tabs to the person's own Notepad and a restored modified tab could hide the school's file; the real-app subjects are now opt-in (JARVIS_SCHOOL_REAL_APPS=on), cleanup never kills the process and only answers a save prompt that names the school's own file, and a review that cannot build its practice task no longer counts against the skill. The gate lowercased every token, so it could not tell git -C (a folder) from git -c (run a setting): -C is now read from the original-case tokens. Keyboard steps went to whatever was in front, so a hotkey could land in another program; the executor now proves the window is in front before every key and refuses otherwise.
dependencies: Python 3.12 standard library; Pillow only for the optional screenshot; the optional uiautomation package for UI Automation (without it ui_tree says so); Windows PowerShell 5.1, winget and Microsoft Defender for the live paths. No new network services, models or paid calls. A teacher model is optional and registered through tools.pcskills.set_teacher with a daily call budget; none is registered by default. Creative/multimedia (area 18): media_duration, media_sample_rate and media_channels read a synthesised WAV with ffprobe, which the gate allows only on one local file with read-only flags. Cross-device (area 16): laptop_hostname, laptop_service_state and laptop_disk_used ask the owner's laptop over key-only ssh; the gate allows only a fixed list of read-only remote commands. Virtual machines (area 21): wsl_distro_name, wsl_linux_release and wsl_linux_kernel ask the real WSL2 Linux; the gate allows only wsl --list and a fixed list of read-only commands inside it. Last areas: gfx_* read the graphics card, driver and screen width; self_* read a school transcript (mastered count, who taught a skill, what is stuck); conv_* ask known facts in casual, worried or follow-up wording. The teacher prompt spells out wsl -d distro -- command (the -- is required) after wsl_linux_release went stuck without it. The self_learned_by question now explains the record layout (name line, then learned_by five lines below) because the teachers could not infer it. Game control (area 19): game_corner and game_tour steer a player in a stand-in game window with arrow, Home/End and PageUp/PageDown keys, graded on the game's own move log. Phone (area 16): phone_paired_count reads a secret-free copy of the pairing record and phone_server_up checks the phone server's HTTP status. The UI teacher prompt now says keyboard tasks use key lines only and shows a keyboard example, because small local models answered the game lessons with a button click. State lives under JARVIS_PC_ROOT (default C:\Jarvis), outside data/ so it is not synced by Syncthing. The school needs a local Ollama server for high school and a configured Gemini key for college; without either it simply does not run that phase.
exercises: 1) python -m pytest tests/test_jarvis_pc_*.py tests/test_pcskills_tool.py tests/test_software.py tests/test_skills_registry.py -q (expect green; 32 skipped on Windows are bash-only). 2) Read docs/JARVIS-PC-CONTROL-SKILLS.md, then run python scripts/pc_diagnose_demo.py 'my pc is slow' and explain which checks ran and which could not. 3) Plan python scripts/pc_install_demo.py --github https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep without --go, list each step's tier, then explain why the download step is T2 and the extract step is T1. 4) Install it with --go, uninstall it with scripts/pc_uninstall_demo.py, undo, and confirm the folder and the zip are both gone each time. 5) In tests/test_pcskills_tool.py, explain why confirmed=true alone never runs an install, and what happens if the plan changes after the person says yes. 7) python -m pytest tests/test_jarvis_pc_school.py tests/test_jarvis_pc_uiact.py tests/test_jarvis_pc_safety_net.py -q (on Windows it also runs every subject's reference answer through the real gate, the practice window and Notepad). 8) python -c "from tools import pcskills; print(pcskills.school().status())" for the report card.
